holdings.thesis: Vistra Corp is the largest competitive power generator in the U.S., operating ~44,000 MW of diversified capacity spanning nuclear, natural gas, solar, coal, and battery storage. The AI data-center buildout and national energy emergency declaration have positioned VST as a primary beneficiary of surging electricity demand. VST is the largest position in the portfolio at ~23% combined across both accounts. However, the stock has pulled back materially from its 52-week high of $219.81, now trading near $140-156, down ~16% over the past 10 days. BofA trimmed its target to $196 while reiterating Buy; Morgan Stanley raised to $212; consensus sits near $225 with 18 analysts at Strong Buy. FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $23.3B with EPS of $9.40. Despite technical sell signals short-term, the long-term demand thesis tied to AI power consumption remains fully intact. Net income is forecast to grow 58% next year vs. the broader sector. The oversized position weight (nearly 1 in 4 dollars) is the key risk, warranting a trim to fund diversification.

SoFi Technologies is a digital-first financial services platform with lending, financial services, and technology (Galileo/Technisys) segments. FY2025 revenue reached $3.58B (+35.6% YoY), and the company revised its 2025 GAAP net income guidance upward to ~$370M, well above prior guidance. Management expects to add at least 3 million new members in 2025, representing ~30% growth. However, following its Q2 2026 earnings beat, the stock fell ~9% on unchanged earnings guidance — a clear red flag. Analyst consensus is Hold (23 analysts), with an average 12-month price target of $20.58 and BofA maintaining Underperform at $16. SOFI's beta of 2.52 makes it volatile. The position is meaningful at 11.2% combined, and the post-earnings drop signals near-term caution. The core digital banking thesis remains valid, but the mixed analyst sentiment and headline sensitivity limit near-term conviction. Moderate position, worth holding but not adding.

AutoZone is a best-in-class auto parts retailer serving both DIY (~69% of domestic sales) and commercial customers, with operations in the U.S., Mexico, and Brazil. Q3 FY2026 delivered record sales of $4.84B (+8.4% YoY), with net income up 5.4%. The company expanded its $1.5B share buyback authorization in June 2026 and continues opening net new stores aggressively. 27 analysts rate it Strong Buy with a $3,950 average price target — implying 30%+ upside from current ~$3,100 levels. However, the stock is down ~19% from its 52-week high of $4,388 and now trading near the bottom of its 52-week range, below its 200-day moving average. The aging U.S. vehicle fleet and tariff-driven deferred vehicle purchases are structural tailwinds for aftermarket parts demand. This is a reasonable defensive-growth position. Only 2 shares held — concentrated in one paper account. AZO is a long-term compounder with a strong moat, though a fiscal Q3 miss vs. buy-side expectations has some analysts cutting targets. Hold.

XRP is Ripple's native token used for fast, low-cost cross-border payments via the XRP Ledger. After hitting a cycle peak near $3.66, XRP has retraced sharply and now trades near $1.06–$1.07 — roughly 70% off highs. The key near-term catalyst, the Senate CLARITY Act (which would permanently classify XRP as a commodity), was set aside on July 27 before the Senate recess and cannot receive a vote until fall 2026, removing a major institutional catalyst. Weak ETF inflows have further reduced institutional buying momentum. Consensus AI forecasts cluster around $1.05–$1.25 for August, with a meaningful 25% probability of a breakdown below $1.00. The TrustWallet holding ($1.13) is effectively dust and not meaningfully integrated. The Kraken position at ~$6,064 remains the real exposure. XRP's institutional business is growing but price appreciation has not followed. The thesis is intact long-term, but risk/reward is compressed near-term with regulatory clarity delayed. Weak near-term, moderate long-term.

Pampa Energía is Argentina's leading integrated energy company, operating across oil & gas, electricity generation (5,472 MW capacity), petrochemicals, and a 22,445 km high-voltage transmission network. Q4 2025 sales rose 16% YoY to $507M, driven by higher crude production and stronger thermal power margins. FY2025 revenue was $2.0B (+6.5% YoY), though earnings fell 39.1% — a meaningful concern. The stock trades at a PE of ~8.5x and analysts have a Buy consensus with a $116 12-month price target, implying 40%+ upside from current ~$83. The key risk is Argentina country risk: currency volatility, regulatory changes under President Milei's economic reforms, and commodity price exposure can move the stock dramatically independent of company fundamentals. However, the Milei reform narrative has broadly been a tailwind for Argentine equities and PAM specifically. Position is speculative but appropriately sized as an EM energy play. Analysts are constructive; insider buying was noted in June 2026.

Tempus AI is a data-driven healthcare AI company focused on precision oncology diagnostics and AI-powered clinical workflows. Revenue was ~$1.27B in 2025 with a stellar 73.5% gross margin, though the company remains loss-making with a -14.4% EBIT margin. In July 2026, Tempus announced a $1.5B acquisition of Personalis, expanding its minimal residual disease (MRD) oncology diagnostics platform — a bold strategic move that caused multiple analysts to trim price targets (BofA to $52, Piper Sandler to $56, BTIG to $70). Q2 2026 revenue was $382.5M, beating consensus. TEM surged ~12% on August 8 following peer Doximity's strong earnings and a new CellCarta CDx lab partnership. 16 analysts rate it Buy with a consensus $62.64 target, ~24% above current price. Earnings August 14 are a near-term catalyst — EPS consensus is -$0.13. With the Personalis deal integration risk, elevated valuation (P/S ~5.8x), and continued losses, this is a high-conviction but high-risk position.

Energy Fuels operates the only active conventional uranium mill in the U.S. (White Mesa Mill) and is aggressively pivoting into rare earth element (REE) separation and critical minerals. In Q1 2026, revenues surged 112% YoY to $35.8M, selling 510K lbs of uranium at $70.04/lb. Uranium hit $100+/lb earlier in 2026 before settling to the $84–87 range. UUUU announced a transformational $1.9B acquisition of Vacuumschmelze (VAC), a German rare earth magnet maker, backed by a $725M conditional U.S. government loan. It also has six long-term uranium supply contracts with U.S. nuclear utilities covering 2027–2032. The 52-week range has swung from $5.45 to $28 — this is a high-beta name. Goldman Sachs cut its target from $29 to $21 but kept Buy. 7 analysts rate it Strong Buy with a $26.13 target, implying 100%+ upside from ~$13 current price. The structural U.S. domestic supply chain narrative makes this a compelling speculative hold, but the VAC deal execution risk is real and meaningful.

NVIDIA is the dominant AI infrastructure company, supplying GPUs that power virtually every major AI workload. At ~$224/share with a $5.4T market cap, NVDA trades at premium multiples reflecting extraordinary growth expectations. Q1 FY2027 revenue came in at $81.6B, ahead of consensus, with Q2 guidance at ~$91B. Wall Street expects 96% revenue growth for Q2 FY2027, with earnings reporting on August 26. 61 analysts rate it Strong Buy with a $302.83 average 12-month target — 35% upside. However, NVDA is up only ~2% YTD in 2026, underperforming the S&P 500 (~7%), partly due to China export restrictions and a late-July semiconductor selloff that erased $1T+ in sector market cap. The position at 5.7% is appropriately sized — not too small to matter, not so large as to be a concentration risk. This remains one of the clearest long-term holds in the portfolio. August 26 earnings are a potential major catalyst.

IREN (formerly Iris Energy) is transitioning aggressively from Bitcoin mining to a vertically integrated AI cloud provider. The company has signed $2.8B in new multi-year AI cloud contracts covering ~85% of its revised 2026 annualized run-rate revenue target of $4B+. It plans to deliver 480 MW of AI cloud capacity in 2026, scaling to 1.2 GW in 2027. The acquisition of Mirantis in August 2026 adds an open-source software layer to its cloud platform, and BofA acquired a 5.8% stake recently — a positive institutional signal. However, the stock is down 43.9% in the past 30 days, and recent quarterly earnings massively missed estimates (-$0.74 EPS vs -$0.22 consensus, revenue $144.8M vs $219.7M expected). 13 analysts hold a Buy consensus with a $76.62 target. The execution gap between the bold vision and near-term financials is alarming. This is high-risk, high-reward — the AI data center pivot is real, but financial performance must catch up. Earnings September 16.

USA Rare Earth is a domestic critical minerals company developing the Round Top rare earth project in West Texas and building a vertically integrated mine-to-magnet supply chain. The stock surged 81% in H1 2026, fueled by $1.6B in federal funding commitments (DOE/DOC), $1.5B in private financing from Inflection Point, and a $2.8B definitive acquisition of Brazil's Serra Verde Group — a major producer of all four magnetic rare earths including high-value dysprosium and terbium. Revenue is still tiny (~$1.6M) and EBITDA losses are deep (~$66.7M/quarter). The company holds ~$1.75B in cash, which provides runway. Roth Capital Buy-rated at $30 (lowered from $40). Stock is up 8.85% as of August 7 and up 85.87% over the past year. This is a pure policy-driven speculative play on de-Chinaification of rare earth supply chains — high risk, but the government backing and supply chain urgency narrative are genuinely compelling. Sized appropriately small at 3.4%.

Chainlink is the dominant decentralized oracle network, providing price feeds for DeFi protocols and CCIP (Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol) for institutional cross-chain transfers. LINK's technology is deeply embedded in DeFi and expanding into bank-grade tokenized real-world asset (RWA) infrastructure. However, LINK trades near $8.33 — far below its ~$52 all-time high — and technical indicators are bearish: the 50-day MA is falling, the 200-day MA is declining, and the weekly trend remains down. August forecasts cluster around $6.58–$10.11. The fundamental disconnect between LINK's growing institutional utility and its price is a persistent feature, not a bug — integration revenue lags adoption by quarters. The CLARITY Act delay also suppresses altcoin sentiment. This is a small speculative position at 2.4%, which is appropriate given the technical weakness. The long-term RWA tokenization thesis makes it worth holding, but not adding at current momentum.

Oklo is a pre-revenue advanced nuclear company developing its Aurora fast-fission microreactor and the Groves Isotope Test Reactor, which achieved first criticality in August 2026 — a genuine milestone. The company has ~$2.5B in liquidity and has received DOE startup authorization. However, OKLO is down ~45% YTD and ~75% from its 52-week high, trading near its 52-week low of $36.61. It is entirely pre-revenue, burning cash, with commercialization years away. The Aurora powerhouse still needs full NRC approval, and regulatory timelines in nuclear are notoriously slow. 25 analysts maintain a Buy rating with a $84.20 consensus target — nearly 100% upside — but that reflects option value in a distant outcome. The call options (OKLO260821C00060000, 5 contracts) in Alpaca add leveraged upside exposure. Combined, the position is 2.2% — appropriately small for a pre-revenue speculative play. The AI data center nuclear power thesis is real; execution risk is enormous.

Cardano is a proof-of-stake Layer-1 blockchain that has completed its Voltaire governance phase, introducing on-chain voting and a $71M community treasury. Over 60% of circulating ADA is staked with no lockup, reducing sell pressure. However, ADA is currently trading near $0.17–$0.19, well below its EMA200 of $0.26 — confirming a dominant downtrend. Bitcoin dominance is elevated at 56.25%, a headwind for altcoin capital rotation. Forecasts for August range from $0.17 to $0.20, with conservative year-end 2026 targets of $0.19–$0.49 depending on the model. ADA's DeFi TVL remains modest and volatile, and the on-chain narrative isn't providing a clear bullish tailwind. The position at 1.1% ($776) is very small — essentially a speculative lottery ticket on Cardano ecosystem growth. Thesis is weak in the near term. Not worth trimming given small size, but no case to add.

Strategy Inc (formerly MicroStrategy) is the world's largest Bitcoin treasury company, operating as a leveraged BTC proxy while also offering AI-powered enterprise analytics software. The company closed July 2026 down ~5% and is consolidating in a symmetrical triangle between $88 support and $108–109 resistance. As of early August 2026, MSTR trades near $92–95. Bitcoin's crypto market pullback has pressured the stock. Cantor Fitzgerald lowered its target to $186 from $212; Barclays lowered to $125. Strategy sold ~$105M in Bitcoin in August to boost USD reserves — an unusual capital management action that spooked some investors. The company reported a large unrealized BTC loss in Q2 2026. The position at 1.0% ($686) is tiny, acting as a de facto Bitcoin proxy lever. Given the small size, it's more of a directional bet on BTC recovery than a meaningful allocation. Hold unless BTC thesis weakens further.

IonQ is the leading pure-play quantum computing company, offering trapped-ion quantum systems via its full-stack platform. Q1 2026 revenue surged 755% YoY to $64.67M, and it raised its FY2026 revenue guidance to $270M at the high end. The company completed the SkyWater Technology acquisition and signed an MOU with Sandia National Laboratories. However, the adjusted EBITDA loss guide is -$310M to -$330M for FY2026, with enormous stock-based comp ($128.5M in Q1 alone). IONQ slid from $69 in June to $41 by August 4, before snapping back ~20%+ in a week. Wall Street average target is ~$68–$70, implying significant upside. IBM's CEO flagging 2026 as the commercial quantum advantage year is a thematic catalyst. Q2 2026 results were released August 5. At only 0.6% of portfolio, this is a small speculative position. The risk/reward is asymmetric — losses are known, upside is enormous if quantum advantage materializes. Appropriately tiny sizing.

SPCX is SpaceX — the world's most dominant launch provider with 80%+ global market share of mass-to-orbit capacity, operator of Starlink across 164+ countries, and owner of xAI (acquired February 2026, which includes the Grok frontier AI model and the X platform). SpaceX IPO'd in June 2026 in the world's largest-ever IPO, making it newly publicly accessible. The stock recently hit $133 (as of August 8), though it faces lock-up expiry volatility and scrutiny over heavy capex. Morningstar notes it trades at a significant valuation premium. This is one of the most compelling long-term holdings thematically — Starlink, reusable rockets, AI infrastructure, and defense contracts — but at 0.3% ($225), the position is dust-level. The position is too small to meaningfully contribute to portfolio returns. Either size it up or let it sit as a conviction starter.

Five call option contracts on OKLO with a $60 strike expiring August 21, 2026. With OKLO trading near $42–43 — well below the $60 strike — these calls are deeply out of the money with ~12 days to expiration. For these to have value at expiry, OKLO would need to surge 40%+ in under two weeks. Given that Q2 earnings were just reported (no revenue, guided loss of -$0.17/share) and the stock is near its 52-week low of $36.61, a near-term catalyst of that magnitude is unlikely without a transformative regulatory announcement (e.g., Aurora DOE approval). These are effectively lottery tickets at this point. The $235 value likely represents time premium that will decay rapidly to near zero by expiry. This position should be monitored daily and closed if any residual premium can be captured ahead of the August 21 expiration.

This is a dust-level holding of 1.000001 XRP worth $1.13 in a TrustWallet account that is not integrated with JCF HQ. It has zero portfolio impact. This should be swept to the main Kraken XRP position or spent on network fees. No thesis warranted at this size — it is effectively zero.

trim: VST (Alpaca paper) — At 20.9% of portfolio in one account alone, VST is dangerously overconcentrated. The stock is down ~16% from recent highs and faces near-term technical headwinds. Trim 20–30 shares in the paper account to reduce combined VST weight from ~23% toward a target of 15–17%, locking in partial gains and freeing capital.

SOFI (Alpaca paper) — With a consensus Hold rating, unchanged earnings guidance causing a 9% post-earnings drop, and BofA at Underperform, the ~9.7% paper allocation is top-heavy for a Hold-rated fintech with 2.52 beta. Consider trimming 60–80 shares to reduce to ~6–7% weight.

OKLO260821C00060000 — These deeply OTM calls expire August 21, 2026. With OKLO near $42 vs. $60 strike, these are 98% likely to expire worthless. Exit any residual premium now rather than letting them decay to zero.

ADA — While small at 1.1%, ADA is in a confirmed downtrend (trading below EMA200), Bitcoin dominance is elevated suppressing altcoin rotation, and the position generates no yield. Consider swapping into a higher-conviction crypto asset or consolidating into XRP.
XRP (TrustWallet) — $1.13 dust position. Send to Kraken or use for gas fees. No portfolio utility whatsoever.
add: SPCX (SpaceX) — The position at $225 (0.3%) is absurdly small for one of the most compelling growth stories of the decade. SpaceX dominates orbital launch, Starlink is a global internet monopoly in its space category, and the xAI acquisition adds frontier AI exposure. Consider building to at least 1.5–2% of portfolio. Post-lockup-expiry volatility may provide a better entry.

NVDA — At 5.7%, NVDA is reasonably sized but given the August 26 earnings catalyst with 96% revenue growth consensus and a $302 average price target, adding ahead of or on earnings weakness is compelling. Consider adding 2–5 fractional shares in Robinhood.

UUUU — The $1.9B Vacuumschmelze acquisition and $725M U.S. government loan commitment are transformational. With 7 analysts at Strong Buy and a $26.13 target vs. ~$13 current price, and UUUU being the only U.S. conventional uranium mill operator, the risk/reward here favors adding on weakness. Consider adding 50–100 shares in Robinhood to bring total to ~9% of portfolio.

VST (Robinhood real money) — While trimming the paper account, consider modestly accumulating real-money VST in Robinhood on dips toward $140 support. The long-term AI power demand thesis and Strong Buy consensus ($225 target) make it a core real-money hold.

Note: Public.com / Roth IRA is NOT reflected in these holdings or rotation suggestions — that account has never been integrated into JCF HQ and should be connected to get a complete cross-account picture.
rotation.summary: The portfolio is thematically well-constructed across AI power (VST, NVDA), healthcare AI (TEM), nuclear/uranium (UUUU, OKLO), rare earth critical minerals (USAR), and crypto (XRP, LINK, ADA, MSTR), but suffers from two structural problems: dangerous concentration in VST (~23% combined) and a fragmented tail of dust-level positions that add complexity without contribution. The week's key developments — VST's technical breakdown from highs, SOFI's post-earnings selloff despite a beat, TEM's Personalis deal sparking analyst target cuts, IREN's massive earnings miss, and XRP's CLARITY Act delay — all argue for defensive rebalancing. Priority actions are trimming VST paper to free capital, closing the worthless OKLO calls before August 21 expiration, rotating ADA dust into XRP, and beginning to build a meaningful SPCX position. NVDA's August 26 earnings with 96% consensus revenue growth is the portfolio's most important near-term catalyst — ensure real-money exposure is not underweight heading into that print.

excluded_accounts: Public.com / Roth IRA (Roth, Spending, Joint, Strategies, Custodial tabs) — never integrated into JCF HQ, so it is NOT reflected below.
